result.markdown: --- title: "08 · Model building" subtitle: "Week 2" --- ::: {.guiding-q} How do I build a good model? ::: ## In this session - Models follow from the research question, not from the data - Choosing predictors and control variables: causal reasoning and DAGs - Non-linear effects with polynomials and transformations - Simulating data from your planned model to check design and power - Writing down the model *before* data collection (link to the course [Open, Replicable, and Ethical Science](../../ores/index.qmd)) ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [Polynomial term](../../glossary.qmd#polynomial), [Power](../../glossary.qmd#power), [Preregistration](../../glossary.qmd#preregistration) ::: ## Learning goals After this session you can - derive a model from a research question and justify each term, - recognise when to include a quadratic term or transform a variable, - run a simple power analysis by simulation. ## Simulate first Power analysis by simulation: how often do we detect a slope of 0.3 with *n* animals? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(8) power_for_n <- function(n, b1 = 0.3, nsim = 500) { mean(replicate(nsim, { x <- rnorm(n); y <- b1 * x + rnorm(n) summary(lm(y ~ x))$coefficients[2, 4] < .05 })) } ns <- seq(10, 120, by = 10) pow <- sapply(ns, power_for_n) plot(ns, pow, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "#1b6f8a", ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Sample size", ylab = "Power") abline(h = .8, lty = 2, col = "#c0392b") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-model-building_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=975} ::: ::: ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R script coming soon - Exercises coming soon ::: ## Reading - McElreath, R. (2020). *Statistical rethinking* (2nd ed.), ch. 5–6 (on confounds and DAGs). CRC Press. - Gelman, Hill & Vehtari (2020), ch. 12 and 16.
